pass_a_gloss: But if anyone, giving in out of much love of life, or out of the softness toward toils, or out of the things thought to be persuasively brought forward by those trying to persuade us toward the worse things, should deny that there is one God and his Christ, and should confess demons or fortunes, let such a one know that he is preparing for the demon a table and filling for Fortune a mixed drink, having forsaken the Lord and forgetting his holy mountain, being about to be subject to these reproofs, as Isaiah wrote it down in this manner: you who forsook me and are forgetting my holy mountain and preparing for the demon a table and filling for Fortune a mixed drink, I will hand you over into a sword, all of you in slaughter will fall; because I called you and you did not obey, I spoke and you disregarded, and you did the evil thing before me and the things I did not wish you picked out. Because of this, these things the Lord, the Lord says: behold, those serving me will eat, but you will hunger; behold, those serving me will drink, but you will thirst; behold, those serving me will be cheered, but you will be shamed; behold, those serving me will leap for joy in good cheer, but you will cry aloud because of the pain of the heart, and from the crushing of spirit you will howl. For you will leave my name for satiety to my chosen ones, but you the Lord will take away. But also if, perceiving what the table of the Lord is, we should wish to partake of it, let us know the word: you are not able to partake of the Lord's table and of a demons' table. But also if, grasping what this is: I will surely not drink from now out of the produce of this vine until that day, until I drink it new in the kingdom of the heavens, we wish to be found with those drinking together with Jesus, let us attend to the word: you are not able to drink a cup of the Lord and a cup of demons. And who, having heard the son of the thunder, John, saying: the one denying the Father and the Son, everyone denying the Son does not even have the Father, the one confessing the Son has the Father too, will not fear through the saying that he is not a Christian to deny the Son, being in the denying of him about not to have the Father? And who would not be urged forward to confess the being a Christian by works and by words, so that he may have the Father too? For the confessing ones have the Father.
pass_b_english: But suppose someone gives way, from a great love of life, or from softness in the face of hardship, or from the arguments, thought persuasive, that are put to us by those who try to win us over to the worse course, and denies that there is one God and his Christ, and confesses demons or Fortunes. Let such a man know that he is preparing “a table for the demon” and filling “a mixed cup for Fortune”, that he has forsaken the Lord and is forgetting his holy mountain, and that he will be liable to these reproofs, which Isaiah wrote down in this way: “But you who have forsaken me and are forgetting my holy mountain, who prepare a table for the demon and fill a mixed cup for Fortune, I will hand you over to the sword; you will all fall in the slaughter. For I called you and you did not answer; I spoke and you paid no heed; you did what was evil before me and chose what I did not want. Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: See, those who serve me will eat, but you will go hungry; see, those who serve me will drink, but you will be thirsty; see, those who serve me will be glad, but you will be put to shame; see, those who serve me will exult with gladness, but you will cry out for pain of heart and wail for a crushed spirit. For you will leave my name to my chosen ones for their fill, but the Lord will destroy you” (Isaiah 65:11-15).

Again, if we understand what the Lord's table is and want to share in it, let us recognise the words, “You cannot share in the Lord's table and in a table of demons” (1 Corinthians 10:21). And if we understand what is meant by “I will not drink from now on of this fruit of the vine until that day, until I drink it new in the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 26:29), and wish to be found among those who drink with Jesus, let us heed the words, “You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and a cup of demons” (1 Corinthians 10:21). Who, hearing John, the son of thunder, say, “He who denies the Father and the Son: everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either; he who confesses the Son has the Father also” (1 John 2:22-23), will not be afraid to deny the Son by saying he is not a Christian, when by denying him he will not have the Father? And who would not be moved to confess that he is a Christian, in deeds and in words, so that he may have the Father as well? For those who confess have the Father.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 40); the old English was a digest: it compressed the Isaiah quotation, lost the opening argument (denial from love of life, softness, or persuasion; confessing demons or Fortunes), and inserted 'I am the vine', which is not in the Greek.
M's doubled verb, printed by Koetschau, is rendered once as 'thus says the Lord, the Lord'; recorded in translator_notes.
'ὅτε ἐκάλεσα' read as 'ὅτι ἐκάλεσα' (LXX, and the usual OCR confusion in this scan): 'For I called you'. '0005' read as 'ὄρος'; 'ὀλολύξετε', 'ἐκλεκτοῖς' read for the OCR forms.
Rendered 'demons or Fortunes' and 'for Fortune' (the deity Tyche), capitalised, since Isaiah's LXX names a deity.
